compliance_deadlines: 2026년 1월 인공지능 기본법 시행 (AI Basic Act enters into force January 2026)
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: The guideline explicitly states it has no legal binding force ('가이드라인 자체는 법적 구속력은 없으나 법상 의무 이행을 지원하기 위한 목적으로 제작') but supports compliance with the legally binding obligations of Article 34 of the AI Basic Act (인공지능 기본법). Obligations under Article 34 include: (1) risk management plan establishment and operation; (2) explainability plan for AI outputs, key criteria, and training data; (3) user protection plan; (4) human oversight of high-impact AI; (5) documentation and retention of safety/reliability measures. High-impact AI domains are enumerated in the AI Basic Act and include energy supply, water treatment, healthcare, medical devices, nuclear facility management, biometric data for criminal investigation, hiring and loan review, transportation, public services decision-making, and student assessment in early/primary/secondary education.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The document's stated rationale centers on protecting citizens' safety and fundamental rights (기본권) from high-impact AI systems. The background section explicitly states the law aims to provide 'legal basis for protecting citizens' safety and fundamental rights alongside AI development.' Operator obligations are framed around human oversight, explainability, user protection, and risk management—all justified by the potential for high-impact AI to significantly affect life, physical safety, and fundamental rights.

evidence_spans.quote: 인공지능 기술의 발전과 함께 국민의 안전과 기본권 보호를 위한 법적 기반을 마련하고자 한다
고영향 인공지능이 사람의 생명 신체의 안전 및 기본권에 중대한 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 점을 고려
